commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA carve-out keyed on the witness exemplar flag `entry_is_line_b` rather than on Section 232 aluminum membership as HTS 9903.01.77's aluminum exception requires, so the surcharge fired and was suppressed on the wrong sets of entries.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 12. Chapter-prefixed steel parameter is ch15_s232_steel_heading_rate; parenthesis depth differs from ch13 only for the placement gate. No other change.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as provenance-only or as mere generalization and could not: the ch15 diff changes two live formula lines in `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`, so the set of entries that receive the Brazil IEEPA surcharge changes — not mechanical. The pre-fix gate keyed the Brazil carve-out on `entry_is_line_b`, the witness's exemplar-line boolean (the module still uses that same flag as the whole formula of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded`), while the rule's own proof atom claims the aluminum exception: "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02." Reading the source through the pinned release confirms the carve-out is article-class membership, not line identity: 9903.01.77 excepts "products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83", and 9903.01.83 is "Articles of iron or steel; derivative articles of iron or steel; articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ... of Brazil". A condition carrying a source excerpt it does not implement, re-grounded here onto the membership predicate, is exactly untraceable_branch; wrong_entity_or_scope is the only rival reading and fits worse because the rule's entity, population, and period are unchanged.

triage.verifier_notes:
1) The first reader's quote is off-target provenance: "The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had" is PR-body text describing PR #1300 as a whole, most of which landed in the PARENT commit a9562cfd ("b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces"). `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` already exists in the pre file at lines 2744/2751, and the steel rule `ch15_s232_steel_heading_rate` already exists pre-fix; the grandparent 2a6bdb01d still had `not entry_is_line_b`. So this commit is the certify pass that fixed a left-behind gate, which strengthens (not weakens) the defect reading: one gate was missed when the rest of the surface was generalized. The decisive evidence is the diff line, not the PR sentence.
2) The second half of the ch15 diff (source string and proof-atom `corpus_citation_path` 9903.81.87/.88 -> 9903.82.02, excerpt text identical, rate still `0.50`) is citation/provenance only and is mechanical under the stated rules; it should not drive the kind. Note this commit did NOT add us/statute/hts/9903.82.02 to `module.source_verification.corpus_citation_paths` — the PR issue comment says that containment gap was caught in a later repair round.
3) Source verification detail for the reviewer: the module's atom cites us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219 for the aluminum exception, but that path in the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS Rev. 3 notes) resolves to an unrelated subheading list — the module is built on a "2026 Rev. 15" vintage and the page locators are stale across revisions (the commit report flags the same problem for 9903.81.x). I confirmed the legal substance instead through the headings themselves (9903.01.77 and 9903.01.83), which is independent of pagination.
4) The fix is correct in direction but partial: 9903.01.83 also carves out iron/steel and derivative steel, wood, vehicles and parts, semiconductors, and copper from the Brazil IEEPA duty, and the post-fix gate excludes only §232 aluminum. A remaining unrepresented_clause defect plausibly survives this commit; that is a separate finding, not a reason to downgrade this one.
